findings.what: Demoting audit_passed=False makes assemble throw away the cleaned OCR page and ship native SUCCESS instead. On the issue's own document class (born-digital, native_text present, VLM OCR) the fabricated URL is gone, but so is the table the VLM actually extracted; the corpus gets flattened native, the page sidecar is restamped SUCCESS/audit_passed=True, and the document stays SUCCESS. The sanitizer-only tests cannot see this.
findings.why:
At main_sha, _winning_page_output returns best_output only when audit_passed is true; otherwise a born-digital page with native_text takes the native branch (manifest.py:355) and ships engine=native / SUCCESS unless a table-distrust flag is set. I reproduced this against commit 4200171: after _sanitize_agentic_page_image_refs, out.text had the marker and no imgur, but _winning_page_output(state, 1) returned native text 'Table 2.3 Public finances

borrowing forecast 2022 2023 2024
' with status=SUCCESS, audit_passed=True, table markdown gone. needs_repair is False because a non-native attempt exists (state.py:115-116), so pages_ok stays true and assemble stamps DocumentStatus.SUCCESS (orchestrator.py:5104-5109). The OBR pages that motivated #225 are exactly this shape. A page that also had a real local figure would lose that too. Fix the seam: keep the OCR body as the winner while demoting, or demote after winner selection — do not flip audit_passed on best_output before assemble.

findings.what: No reverse-regression assertion that a legitimate image ref still ships through assemble/_winning_page_output. The three reverse tests only inspect the PageOutput mutated by _sanitize_agentic_page_image_refs. That is the naive test the brief warned about: a strip-too-much (or swap-to-native) fix still passes them.
findings.why: test_url_present_in_the_source_pdf_still_ships and test_local_asset_socr_wrote_still_ships never call _winning_page_output, _canonical_body, or _phase_assemble. Combined with finding 1 they are vacuous as corpus-level guards. Issue #225's suggested minimum is that a real local asset and a URL the PDF itself carries must still ship; that property is untested on the path that actually writes pages/NNN.md.

findings.what: A provenanced URL in CommonMark title syntax is treated as fabricated and stripped: ![Chart](https://example.com/chart.png "Official chart") when the PDF's LINK_URI is exactly that URL.
findings.why: The new matcher is the same [^)]+ shape as OutputNormalizer._RE_MD_IMAGE at main_sha. The title is swallowed into the target, normalize_url does not equal the annotation, and the ref is replaced by the marker. Reproduced against 4200171: source_url_index contained https://example.com/chart.png; redact_fabricated_image_refs removed the image. That is a real URL the PDF carries, i.e. the reverse regression the brief ranked first. The reverse test only uses ![Chart 2.3](url) with no title.

findings.what: Issue #225 said fail the page, not warn. The PR demotes SUCCESS→WARNING and, on the born-digital path, assemble then restamps SUCCESS. Cardinal-rule surfacing is overstated.
findings.why: PR body table claims page/metadata/document/CLI all carry the signal. On a scanned page, needs_repair becomes True so the document is AUDIT_FAILED and CLI prints the yellow audit warning — that path works. On the OBR born-digital path, pages_ok is True, result.status is SUCCESS, metadata is COMPLETED, CLI prints Success, and the note in final_result.error is a dim line on a green run. CLI only non-zeros AUDIT_FAILED when LOST_CONTENT_NOTE is in result.error (cli.py:454-466); a fabrication note does not trip that. Phase-major 'no per-page demotion' is honestly disclosed; the agentic born-digital SUCCESS restamp is not.
